_instrucciones: This is NOT CV data — it's just a guide for whoever fills in this file (you or an AI assistant like ChatGPT/Claude). Delete this '_instrucciones' key before importing, or leave it: the app ignores it safely either way. Full guide: paste this file to your AI assistant along with your old CV, your exported LinkedIn profile, or a list of your experience, and ask it to fill in every field while following this exact shape (same keys, same types: lists stay lists, text stays text). Then: in the app, click the 'Importar datos' button at the top right, pick the completed .json, done — your CV builds itself. Fields you can leave as-is (they're design settings, changeable later from the app): modelo, modeloCarta, tema, fuente, iconos, colorOscuro, colorClaro, escalaFoto, escalaIconos, idiomaCv, tipoDocumento. Valid values — modelo: 'modelo1' through 'modelo20'. modeloCarta: 'carta1' through 'carta6' (only used if tipoDocumento is 'carta'). tema: 'turquesa', 'azul', 'verde', 'bordo', 'violeta', 'coral'. idiomaCv: 'en' or 'es' (the language of the printed CV's SECTION TITLES, not your content). tipoDocumento: 'cv' or 'carta' — which document this template generates (also changeable from the app). contacto[].tipo: 'telefono', 'email', 'ubicacion', 'linkedin', 'web'. contacto[].url is optional, only has an effect on the 'linkedin' type (turns your name into a link to your profile). experiencia[].empresaUrl is optional (turns the company name into a link to its site). experiencia[].ubicacion is optional (the city and country where you worked that role, e.g. 'Buenos Aires, Argentina' — shown next to the company name; leave it empty if you don't want it shown). The 'carta' block holds the cover letter's own fields (name/contact/photo come from the rest of the file). Everything else is free text in whatever language you want (English recommended, it's the CV standard). 'foto' stays null — the photo is uploaded separately, by dragging it into the app, it doesn't go in this file.
puesto: Your current job title (e.g. Senior Backend Engineer)
subtitulo: Optional short tag next to your title (e.g. a language level like C1, or leave empty)

contacto.etiqueta: Optional short label (e.g. country code like US)

perfil: A 3-5 sentence professional summary: who you are, your years of experience, your specialty/focus area, and what kind of impact or track record you bring. Write it in first-person-implied style (no 'I' — CVs usually drop the subject), like: 'Senior backend engineer with 8+ years building...'

habilidades.texto: A hard/technical skill (e.g. Python, React, AWS, SQL) — group related tools into one line if you have many, e.g. 'CI/CD — GitHub Actions & GitLab CI'

blandas.texto: A soft skill (e.g. Effective communication, Critical thinking, Team leadership)

bullets.texto: Degree name, honors, or a relevant detail

certificaciones.subtitulo: Optional one-line detail about the certification

logros.texto: One standout achievement, ideally with a number/result (e.g. 'Reduced deploy time by 40% by...')

experiencia.ubicacion: City, Country (e.g. Buenos Aires, Argentina) — optional, leave empty to hide it
experiencia.fecha: Free-text date range, e.g. JAN 2023 - PRESENT
experiencia.rol: Your job title at this company
experiencia.descripcion: 1-3 sentences about the company/team context and your overall mandate in this role.

bullets.texto: A specific responsibility or achievement, ideally with concrete numbers/impact.
Another bullet — aim for 4-8 per job, each one a single clear sentence.

herramientas.etiqueta: A category label (e.g. Automation, Cloud & Infrastructure)
herramientas.valor: Comma-separated tools/tech used in that category

carta.destinatario: Optional — e.g. 'Hiring Manager' or a specific recruiter's name
carta.fecha: Optional — leave empty to use today's date automatically
carta.cuerpo: The letter body — write it as one or more paragraphs separated by a blank line (each blank line becomes a new paragraph in the printed letter).
